The passages do not give the total "restructuring and other" line for 2023 or 2022, and they do not give a single explanation of the year-over-year change. They do show the main components:

- **Happy Returns sale (2023):** a pre-tax gain of $339 million, net of transaction costs, recorded in restructuring and other [1]. This offset other charges in the line.
- **2023 workforce reduction:** restructuring charges of $122 million, mainly employee severance and benefits, substantially completed by Q4 2023 [6]. The 2022 workforce reduction charges were $121 million, so the two years are nearly the same on this item [5].
- **Other 2023 items:** about $74 million of losses on loans and interest receivable held for sale [1], a $17 million gain on an owned property sale and a $14 million loss on another owned property [1].
- **Lease impairments:** $61 million in 2023 [3], compared with $81 million in 2022 [4].

The passages do not net these items into a total or compare the two years' line totals.
